searchText: Idea for running two EL nodes: 1. EL1 is connected to the network, downloads new blocks and sometimes produces one for a CL validator. 2. EL2 is offline. 3. When EL1 gets a new valid block it also pushes it to EL2 (via import) and checks if EL2 confirms it is valid. 4. For blocks produced by EL1 it also pushes it to EL2 for validation. 5. In case of any disagreement between EL1 and EL2 the CL validator stops attesting. Doesn't this increase the impact of bugs in a certain EL client dramatically and impact client diversity? The goal is to stop attestation in case of bug instead of attesting to a buggy output. If you want to do something like that you should put it in to middleware rather than have execution clients attempt to talk to each other. There is The Minority Client which is this kind of middleware, https://github.com/karalabe/minority. I guess it's work in progress and any contribution would be very much appreciated

excerpts.content:
Idea for running two EL nodes:
1. EL1 is connected to the network, downloads new blocks and sometimes produces one for a CL validator.
2. EL2 is offline.
3. When EL1 gets a new valid block it also pushes it to EL2 (via import) and checks if EL2 confirms it is valid.
4. For blocks produced by EL1 it also pushes it to EL2 for validation.
5. In case of any disagreement between EL1 and EL2 the CL validator stops attesting.
